verbalization: Niraparib, a poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor, is associated with the treatment of primary peritoneal serous/papillary carcinoma, which in turn is linked to malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary. This suggests a potential pathway where Niraparib may influence the progression or treatment of ovarian tumors through its mechanism of action. The evidence implies that Niraparib is used in combination with bevacizumab, a vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitor, which is known to target tumor angiogenesis. The integration of these two drugs suggests a possible synergistic effect in targeting tumor growth, possibly through PARP inhibition and VEGF blockade. The relationship between Niraparib and malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary is thus supported by the sequential indications, highlighting the role of PARP inhibitors in the treatment of ovarian tumors.
